7530-the-renascence-of-hebrew-literature.title: The Renascence Of Hebrew Literature 1743 1885
7530-the-renascence-of-hebrew-literature.creator: Unknown
7530-the-renascence-of-hebrew-literature.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It was long believed that Hebrew had no place among the modern languages as a literary vehicle. The circumstance that the Jews of Western countries had given up the use of their national language outside of the synagogue was not calculated to discredit the belief.

75563-cedar-chests-how-to-make-them.title: Copyright 1918-1921
75563-cedar-chests-how-to-make-them.creator: The Bruce Publishing Company
75563-cedar-chests-how-to-make-them.description: A book by The Bruce Publishing Company. When America was settled, one of its most valued natural resources was found in the red cedar belt of the South. Settlers migrating to this region found the straight cedar logs perfectly suited to cabin construction, consequently the best trees were felled and utilized in the building of America’s first homes. As times went on and the settlers prospered, the logs were taken from the houses, and assembled into barns, frame construction taking their place in the homes.

arxiv-2007-14525.title: Acutely Triangulated, Stacked, and Very Ununfoldable Polyhedra
arxiv-2007-14525.creator: Erik D. Demaine, Martin L. Demaine, David Eppstein
arxiv-2007-14525.description: Abstract We present new examples of topologically convex edge-ununfoldable polyhedra, i.e., polyhedra that are combinatorially equivalent to convex polyhedra, yet cannot be cut along their edges and unfolded into one planar piece without overlap. One family of examples is acutely triangulated , i.e., every face is an acute triangle. Another family of examples is stacked , i.e.

arxiv-2103-07227.title: From the SpaceX Starlink megaconstellation to the search for Type-I civilizations
arxiv-2103-07227.creator: Osmanov Z.N
arxiv-2103-07227.description: Abstract Here we extrapolate the idea of launching SpaceX’s Starlink satellites and study the possibility of building planetary megastructures (either designed as solid objects or as a web of satellites) by Type-I civilizations and the consequent detection of their techno-signatures.

arxiv-2108-13838.title: The Interaction Flow Editor: A New Human-Robot Interaction Rapid Prototyping Interface
arxiv-2108-13838.creator: Matthew Huggins, Anastasia K. Ostrowski, Andrew Rapo, Eric Woudenberg, Cynthia Breazeal, Hae Won Park
arxiv-2108-13838.description: Abstract Human-robot interaction can be regarded as a flow between users and robots. Designing good interaction flows takes a lot of effort and needs to be field tested. Unfortunately, the interaction flow design process is often very disjointed, with users experiencing prototypes, designers forming those prototypes, and developers implementing them as independent processes.

arxiv-2208-03775.title: Video-based Human Action Recognition using Deep Learning: A Review
arxiv-2208-03775.creator: Hieu H. Pham, Louahdi Khoudour, Alain Crouzil, Pablo Zegers, Sergio A. Velastin
arxiv-2208-03775.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hieu H. Pham, Louahdi Khoudour, Alain Crouzil, Pablo Zegers, Sergio A. Velastin. Human action recognition is an important application domain in computer vision. Its primary aim is to accurately describe human actions and their interactions from a previously unseen data sequence acquired by sensors. The ability to recognize, understand and predict complex human actions enables the construction of many important applications such as intelligent surveillance systems, human-computer interfaces, health care, security and military applications.

arxiv-2303-16133.title: Exposing and Addressing Cross-Task Inconsistency in Unified Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2303-16133.creator: Adyasha Maharana Amita Kamath Christopher Clark Mohit Bansal Aniruddha Kembhavi
arxiv-2303-16133.description: Abstract As general purpose vision models get increasingly effective at a wide set of tasks, it is imperative that they be consistent across the tasks they support. Inconsistent AI models are considered brittle and untrustworthy by human users and are more challenging to incorporate into larger systems that take dependencies on their outputs.

arxiv-2308-04748.title: Fuzz4All : Universal Fuzzing with Large Language Models Conference: 2024 IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering; April 14–20, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 2024 IEEE/ACM 46th International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE ’24), April 14–20, 2024, Lisbon, Portugal DOI: 10.114
arxiv-2308-04748.creator: Chunqiu Steven Xia, Matteo Paltenghi, Jia Le Tian, Michael Pradel, Lingming Zhang
arxiv-2308-04748.description: Abstract . Fuzzing has achieved tremendous success in discovering bugs and vulnerabilities in various software systems. Systems under test (SUTs) that take in programming or formal language as inputs, e.g., compilers, runtime engines, constraint solvers, and software libraries with accessible APIs, are especially important as they are fundamental building blocks of software development.

arxiv-2502-16941.title: Gaussian Difference: Find Any Change Instance in 3D Scenes
arxiv-2502-16941.creator: Binbin Jiang 1 , Rui Huang 1 , Qingyi Zhao 1 , Yuxiang Zhang 1
arxiv-2502-16941.description: Abstract Instance-level change detection in 3D scenes presents significant challenges, particularly in uncontrolled environments lacking labeled image pairs, consistent camera poses, or uniform lighting conditions. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a novel approach for detecting changes in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2503-00990.title: Maximum Percolation Time on the q-ary hypercube Thanks: Institute for Systems Research and Department of ECE, University of Maryland, College Park, MD 20742, USA, fengxing@terpmail.umd.edu. Supported in part by NSF grant CCF 2330909.
arxiv-2503-00990.creator: Fengxing Zhu
arxiv-2503-00990.description: Abstract . We consider the 2 2 -neighbor bootstrap percolation process on the n n -dimensional q q -ary hypercube with vertex set V = { 0 , 1 , … , q − 1 } n V=\{0,1,\dots,q-1\}^{n} and edges connecting the pairs at Hamming distance 1 1 .

arxiv-2503-21454.title: Dynamic scaling and Family-Vicsek universality in S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) quantum spin chains
arxiv-2503-21454.creator: Cătălin Paşcu Moca, Balázs Dóra, Doru Sticlet, Angelo Valli, Tomaž Prosen, Gergely Zaránd
arxiv-2503-21454.description: Abstract The Family-Vicsek scaling is a fundamental framework for understanding surface growth in non-equilibrium classical systems, providing a universal description of temporal surface roughness evolution. While universal scaling laws are well established in quantum systems, the applicability of Family-Vicsek scaling in quantum many-body dynamics remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2507-06376.title: SLDB: An End-To-End Heterogeneous System-on-Chip Benchmark Suite for LLM-Aided Design
arxiv-2507-06376.creator: Elisavet Lydia Alvanaki, Kevin Lee, Luca P. Carloni
arxiv-2507-06376.description: Abstract Over the last few years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a valuable tool for Electronic Design Automation (EDA). State-of-the-art research in LLM-aided design has demonstrated the ability of LLMs to generate syntactically correct RTL code, showcasing encouraging prospects for integrating AI into the hardware design process.

arxiv-2508-15483.title: HebID: Detecting Social Identities in Hebrew-language Political Text
arxiv-2508-15483.creator: Guy Mor-Lan, Naama Rivlin-Angert, Yael R. Kaplan, Tamir Sheafer, Shaul R. Shenhav
arxiv-2508-15483.description: Abstract Political language is deeply intertwined with social identities. While social identities are often shaped by specific cultural contexts and expressed through particular uses of language, existing datasets for group and identity detection are predominantly English-centric, single-label and focus on coarse identity categories.

arxiv-2601-07327.title: How to predict creativity ratings from written narratives: A comparison of co-occurrence and textual forma mentis networks
arxiv-2601-07327.description: Abstract This tutorial paper provides a step-by-step workflow for building and analysing semantic networks from short creative texts. We introduce and compare two widely used text-to-network approaches: word co-occurrence networks and textual forma mentis networks (TFMNs). We also demonstrate how they can be used in machine learning to predict human creativity ratings.

pmc-11340224.title: Lamin A/C facilitates DNA damage response by modulating ATM signaling and homologous recombination pathways
pmc-11340224.creator: Seong-jung Kim, Su Hyung Park, Kyungjae Myung, Kyoo-young Lee
pmc-11340224.description: Lamin A/C, a core component of the nuclear lamina, forms a mesh-like structure beneath the inner nuclear membrane. While its structural role is well-studied, its involvement in DNA metabolism remains unclear. We conducted sequential protein fractionation to determine the subcellular localization of early DNA damage response (DDR) proteins.

pmc-11522910.title: Personalized delayed anticoagulation therapy alleviates postoperative bleeding in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) patients
pmc-11522910.creator: Xuefeng Luo, Dehua Wang, Wei Xu, Jing Zou, Runxing Kang, Tao Zhang, Xi Liang, Junyi Liao, Wei Huang
pmc-11522910.description: PurposeEcchymosis is one of the most common complications following total knee arthroplasty (TKA), which is closely related to postoperative bleeding. However, it is still controversial whether anticoagulation treatment should be continued for postoperative ecchymosis patients. We suppose that personalized delayed anticoagulation therapy could be beneficial for decreasing postoperative bleeding.

pmc-11611742.title: USP10 drives cancer stemness and enables super-competitor signalling in colorectal cancer
pmc-11611742.creator: Michaela Reissland, Oliver Hartmann, Saskia Tauch, Jeroen M. Bugter, Cristian Prieto-Garcia, Clemens Schulte, Sinah Loebbert, Daniel Solvie, Eliya Bitman-Lotan, Ashwin Narain, Anne-Claire Jacomin, Christina Schuelein-Voelk, Carmina T. Fuss, Nikolett Pahor, Carsten Ade, Viktoria Buck, Michael Potente
pmc-11611742.description: The contribution of deubiquitylating enzymes (DUBs) to β-Catenin stabilization in intestinal stem cells and colorectal cancer (CRC) is poorly understood. Here, and by using an unbiassed screen, we discovered that the DUB USP10 stabilizes β-Catenin specifically in APC-truncated CRC in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-11715891.title: Diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease using highly specific amyloid and tau positron emission tomography
pmc-11715891.creator: Hiroshi Matsuda, Haruo Hanyu, Chikako Kaneko, Tensho Yamao
pmc-11715891.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe Alzheimer's disease (AD) research framework has advocated defining AD as a function of the presence or absence of amyloidopathy (A), tauopathy (T), and neurodegeneration/neuronal injury (N) biomarkers, as well as the clinical syndrome. Recent advances have made it possible to perform A/T/N classification in vivo using neuroimaging techniques such as amyloid positron emission tomography (PET), tau PET, and MRI or fluorodeoxyglucose PET.

pmc-11963957.title: Social Risk Profile and Cardiovascular‐Kidney‐Metabolic Syndrome in US Adults
pmc-11963957.creator: Jingkuo Li, Lubi Lei, Wei Wang, Wenbo Ding, Yanwu Yu, Boxuan Pu, Yue Peng, Yinchu Li, Lihua Zhang, Yuanlin Guo
pmc-11963957.description: BackgroundPoor cardiovascular‐kidney‐metabolic (CKM) health is associated with premature mortality and excess morbidity in the United States. Adverse social conditions have a prominent impact on cardiometabolic diseases during the life course. We aim to examine the association between social risk profile (SRP) and CKM multimorbidity among US adults.

pmc-12524649.title: Exploring Clinical Governance Interventions and Organisational Learning in Public Hospitals in South Africa’s Eastern Cape and Mpumalanga Provinces: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
pmc-12524649.creator: Kedibone Maake, Wezile Chitha, Sibusiso C Nomatshila, Sikhumbuzo A Mabunda, John Capitman
pmc-12524649.description: Safeguarding patient and personnel safety and improving care quality has emerged as a critical priority for healthcare systems globally. In response to persistent challenges in healthcare delivery, many countries have adopted clinical governance frameworks and organisational learning processes to strengthen accountability and promote continuous improvement.

pmc-12530411.title: Clinical and epidemiological factors affecting donor corneal endothelial cell density
pmc-12530411.creator: Eden Amir, Dean David Lichter, Netanel Corem, Abraham Solomon
pmc-12530411.description: Background/aimsThe limited availability of corneal donors poses a significant challenge to meeting transplantation demands. Factors such as advanced donor age and prior cataract surgery are known to reduce donor corneal quality, yet a predictive system for resource optimisation is lacking.

pmc-12700814.title: Domestic abuse experienced by healthcare practitioners: what about dentists and dental care professionals? A systematised review
pmc-12700814.creator: Lorna K MacNab, Paul Cannon, Clare McFeely, Sandi Dheensa
pmc-12700814.description: Introduction Domestic abuse (DA) is a significant global public health issue. It is recognised that dentists and dental care professionals (DCPs) play a key role in recognising and responding to abuse in patients; however, it is rarely acknowledged that they, personally, may be DA victim/survivors.

pmc-13030974.title: A robust method for on-chip production and manipulation of lipid vesicles by inverted emulsion
pmc-13030974.creator: Naresh Yandrapalli, David T. Gonzales, Weihua Leng, Cynthia Alsayyah, Nurzhan Abdukarimov, Robert Ernst, T.-Y. Dora Tang
pmc-13030974.description: SummaryLipid vesicles are important as minimal model systems for cellular compartmentalization. They drive major advances in deciphering biological mechanisms by molecular reconstitution; provide rational solutions for primitive compartmentalization in origin-of-life studies; form the basis of synthetic cells and drug delivery vehicles. The emulsion method is a well-established route for producing bilayer lipid vesicles.

The open-bite group consisted of 117 patients (69 women and 48 men; average age 24.05 ± 12.

pmc-13233533.title: Cross domain consistency of aesthetic preference-driven social behavior
pmc-13233533.creator: Trung Quang Pham, Junichi Chikazoe
pmc-13233533.description: IntroductionAesthetic preference is a primary driver of social behavior in the digital era, yet the extent to which these preferences remain consistent across disparate domains remains poorly understood.MethodsWe hypothesize that aesthetic judgment is governed by a domain-invariant latent structure, such that individuals who exhibit similar preferences in one category will demonstrate comparable alignment in seemingly unrelated domains.

pmc-13614967.creator: Saeid Kholghi, Georg Northoff
pmc-13614967.description: Schizophrenia is associated with deficits in input processing, but the underlying neural dynamics of this deficit remain unclear.
